title: Lesson Plan — A Letter to God + Dust of Snow + Fire and Ice (Class 10 CBSE English)
subject: English
objectives: Recall the plot of 'A Letter to God' and its setting in Mexico.
Analyse the central irony of the story and the contrast between Lencho and the postmaster.
Explain the message of 'Dust of Snow' and the symbolic reversal Frost achieves.
Explain Frost's argument in 'Fire and Ice' linking natural forces to human emotions.
Identify themes that unify the three pieces — faith, mood, destruction, the power of small things.
Use new vocabulary in writing and discussion.
prerequisites: Familiarity with reading short stories and poems from Class 9.
Knowledge of basic literary terms: theme, character, symbol, rhyme, irony.
materials: Printed copy of the story and the two poems (the NCERT textbook)
Picture cards: a hailstorm, a Mexican farm, a crow on a tree, fire and ice
Vocabulary flashcards (hailstorm, crestfallen, resolute, deluge, amiable, perish, suffice, rued)

activities.description: Hook: 'If you could write a letter to God asking for one thing, what would it be? Take a few responses; introduce Lencho's letter.
Read 'A Letter to God' aloud in sections, with students taking turns. After each section, discuss what just happened.

Cover four blocks: (i) plot + characters of 'A Letter to God'; (ii) themes — faith, irony, perception; (iii) 'Dust of Snow' — symbolism, mood change, ABAB rhyme; (iv) 'Fire and Ice' — fire = desire, ice = hate, philosophical tone.
teacher_actions: Sketch character map of the story.
Read each poem aloud and decode.
Connect the three pieces — power of small things.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions covering plot recall, vocabulary, poem analysis and a short answer on irony.
Exit ticket: 4 quick questions, one from each block.
Homework: write a 5-line paragraph on 'A small moment that lifted my mood'.

homework: Write a 5-line paragraph: 'A small moment that lifted my mood'.
Memorise either 'Dust of Snow' or 'Fire and Ice' and recite tomorrow.
List 5 examples of irony from a TV show, news article or another story you know.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Run a 10-question quiz next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on irony in 'A Letter to God' using a 5-point rubric.
references: NCERT Class 10 — First Flight, Chapter 1: A Letter to God + Dust of Snow + Fire and Ice.
